clauses.reason: Enacting words introducing Sec. 1 to 3. No separate command; exhausted with them when the order took effect on signing, 1991-07-25.

Revokes EO 12723 and EO 12725 and states that the revocation does not affect the national emergency declared in EO 12722. Sec. 3 makes the order effective immediately, so the revocation was performed on signing, 1991-07-25, and the command is exhausted on that date. The statement about EO 12722 limits the revocation and creates no continuing duty.

Lead-in to the savings list: the revocation does not affect the three listed categories. Fixed to the effective date (July 25, 1991); the protected effects are accrued and are treated under savings. Ends 1991-07-25.

Saves any action taken or proceeding pending and not finally concluded on the effective date. The class is fixed at the effective date, 1991-07-25; the saved proceedings continue under their own law, not under this order.
Saves any action or proceeding based on an act committed before the effective date. The class is fixed at 1991-07-25 and the saved actions continue under their own law.

Saves rights and duties that matured and penalties incurred before the effective date. The class is fixed at 1991-07-25; the saved rights, duties and penalties are accrued consequences, not commands of this order.
Makes the order effective immediately, which fixes the performance date of the revocation at signing, 1991-07-25. The clause is spent on that date.

research_rationale:
EO 12771 of July 25, 1991 (Revoking Earlier Orders With Respect to Kuwait), read in full in the held Federal Register text (56 FR 35993, Federal Register of July 29, 1991; machine-extracted text layer). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1991-07-25). Sec. 1 revokes EO 12723 and EO 12725 and states that the revocation does not affect the national emergency declared in EO 12722; Sec. 2 preserves pending actions, proceedings based on earlier acts, and matured rights and incurred penalties; Sec. 3 makes the order effective immediately. Legal reading: the revocation is a one-time act performed when the order took effect on signing, July 25, 1991, so the command is exhausted by performance on that date; the surviving consequences (the revoked orders stay revoked; saved actions and rights) are separated from the exhausted command and are treated under savings. Inventory: the dossier's seven clauses (lead, Sec. 1, Sec. 2 with items (a) to (c), Sec. 3) cover every operative sentence; the findings paragraph before the lead is recital. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 0. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; the only held text citing this order is its own Federal Register text.

Those preserved effects are accrued consequences of the revoked orders and remain in force by their own terms; the national emergency declared in EO 12722 continues under that order, not this one. Nothing in EO 12771 commands anything after July 25, 1991.
